title: Host Accounts Superhost Decision: Figures Compared with the Standards and the Resulting Tier
content:
# Superhost Programme — Comparison Sheet for a Superhost Decision (Host Accounts)

## The comparison

A Superhost decision on an individual Host Accounts holder's assessment meets the Superhost standards when **all four** of the following hold:

1. the decision's rating figure is at least the Superhost minimum average guest rating;
2. the decision's response figure is at least the Superhost minimum message response rate;
3. the assessment's recorded cancellation rate is below the Superhost cancellation-rate ceiling;
4. the decision's stays figure reaches the Superhost completed-stays standard, **or** reaches the long-stay completed-stays standard with the assessment's recorded completed nights reaching the long-stay completed-nights standard.

The standards are the published Superhost standards of the account's tier.

## The figures

| Figure | What it is |
|---|---|
| Rating figure | The average rating recorded at the decided assessment |
| Response figure | The decided assessment's response rate, being the response rate recorded at that assessment |
| Cancellation rate | The cancellation rate recorded at the decided assessment |
| Stays figure | The completed stays recorded at the decided assessment |
| Completed nights | The completed nights recorded at the decided assessment |

The decided assessment is the Superhost assessment being decided — the account's most recent Superhost assessment, with its assessment date.

## The result

A met decision records the assessment as met with the tier effect promoted and gives the account the Superhost tier, with Superhost status counted from the date of the decision. Any other decision records it as not met with the tier effect unchanged and leaves the account a Standard Host.

## Decision table

| Rating figure at least the minimum | Response figure at least the minimum | Cancellation rate below the ceiling | Stays standard reached by either route | Outcome recorded | Tier effect | Account tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Met | Promoted | Superhost, from the decision date |
| No | any | any | any | Not met | Unchanged | Standard Host |
| any | No | any | any | Not met | Unchanged | Standard Host |
| any | any | No | any | Not met | Unchanged | Standard Host |
| any | any | any | No | Not met | Unchanged | Standard Host |

## The stays standard by route

| Stays figure reaches the completed-stays standard | Stays figure reaches the long-stay completed-stays standard | Recorded nights reach the long-stay nights standard | Stays standard reached |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | — | — | Yes |
| No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| No | Yes | No | No |
| No | No | any | No |

## Worked decision (hypothetical recorded figures, compared with the published standards)

An assessment recorded at an average rating of 4.83 stars, a response rate of 91.20%, a cancellation rate of 0.80%, 9 completed stays and 118 completed nights: the rating, response and cancellation figures clear their standards; 9 stays do not reach the completed-stays standard but do reach the long-stay stays standard, with 118 nights reaching the long-stay nights standard. The decision is met: the assessment is recorded as met and promoted, and the account becomes a Superhost from the decision date. With a recorded response rate of 88.40% instead, the response figure falls short and the decision is not met: recorded as not met, unchanged, and the account stays a Standard Host.
